complexity_scope.guarantee: Certified residual-interface guarantee on every compatible strongly monotone instance; false radius trials are capped and may fail safely.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: Fixed public implementation constants chosen recursively; may reflect fixed exponents, not instance parameters or dimension. No arithmetic-cost or free unknown-operator resolvent claim.
complexity_scope.oracle: Exact feasible order-p jets, all nested original queries counted. Evaluating affine-regularized G from F costs one original-F query plus known data.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Explicit evaluated genuine normal certificate of norm <=delta in original domain X.
complexity_scope.regime: Fixed p and fixed alpha,b in the stated interface scope; all positive L_p,D,mu,delta and all feasible anchors.
complexity_scope.resource: Worst-case total original-query cap, including certificate evaluations, all stages, all guesses and descendants.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Upper-interface reduction witnessed by Algorithm 3 with Algorithm 4 as its trial.

content.intended_use: Acyclic abstract-interface reduction: consume A_{alpha,b}; do not assume any future hierarchy implementation of A.

proofs.full_local_argument: First prove (5.5). Set nstar=-G(zstar) in N_X(zstar). Normal-cone monotonicity follows directly from <n,zstar-x><=0 and <nstar,x-zstar><=0, giving <n-nstar,x-zstar>>=0. Adding mu-strong monotonicity of G gives <G(x)+n,x-zstar>>=mu||x-zstar||^2. Cauchy–Schwarz and division by ||x-zstar|| when nonzero yield mu||x-zstar||<=||G(x)+n||; at x=zstar the inequality is immediate. Now fix a valid R and set a_j=R/2^j. Algorithm 4 initializes z=w and sigma_j=max(delta,mu a_j/2). Inductively, if ||z-zstar||<=a_j and the stage is nonfinal, the abstract residual guarantee and (5.5) give ||y-zstar||<=sigma_j/mu=a_j/2=a_{j+1}. Thus the next promise is valid. At the first stage with mu a_j/2<=delta, the delta call returns the required evaluated certificate. The number of calls is O(1+log_+(mu R/delta)). Each call has sigma_j>=mu a_j/2, hence Q_j=L_p a_j^p/sigma_j<=2L_p a_j^(p-1)/mu. Nonconstant powers therefore form a convergent geometric series for fixed alpha>0. A false initial promise need not give these distance invariants, but the same finite predetermined stage radii and caps still bound its query count. Any failed subcall immediately abandons the trial, and any accepted output remains a genuine checked certificate. Next set rho=(mu/L_p)^(1/(p-1)) and apply AdaptiveStrong with R=min(D,2^ell rho), restarting every trial from original w and never repeating D. The first valid guess succeeds because every promised stage is valid; no valid stage is interrupted prematurely under its interface cap. If rho>=D there is one trial and kappa_D<=1. Otherwise the largest necessary guess is <=2 max(r,rho); consequently L_p R^(p-1)/mu<=2^(p-1)max(1,L_p r^(p-1)/mu). There are O_p(L_S) guesses, since D/rho=kappa_D^(1/(p-1)). To bound all stage logarithms, each initial guess has D/R<=max(1,D/rho). If a trial has a nonfinal stage before its final stage, its final radius is >delta/mu: its predecessor was nonfinal and had mu(2a_final)/2>delta. Thus every stage in such a trial has D/a_j<mu D/delta. If the initial stage is already final, D/a_j=D/R<=max(1,D/rho). In either case D/a_j is bounded by max(1,D/rho,mu D/delta), whose logarithm is O_p(L_S). Also Q_j<=L_p D^p/delta since sigma_j>=delta and a_j<=D. Hence L_A(a_j,sigma_j)<=C_p L_S at every stage, including invalid trials. There are O(L_S) stages because R<=D. Summing the geometric nonconstant terms and the additive per-stage costs gives at most C_p[1+(L_p R^(p-1)/mu)^alpha]L_S^(b+1) per trial; the constants may depend on the fixed alpha,b. Summing O_p(L_S) guesses and substituting the largest-radius bound yields C_p[1+(L_p r^(p-1)/mu)^alpha]L_S^(b+2). At r=0 the first guess already covers the distance and the same estimate uses the additive convention. Every original query is charged to every active ancestor before it occurs, so this sum also controls composed capped implementations. Final acceptance includes the saved evaluated G(y), and all normals are in N_X. This proves the reduction from the abstract interface without any future hierarchy dependency.
map: Equation (5.5): strong monotonicity turns a genuine normal certificate into a distance upper bound.
Algorithm 4 halves a valid promise until the final delta stage; all false-promise stages still have finite interruptible caps.
Geometric radius guesses bound the largest required radius by 2 max(r,rho), or D when rho>=D.
Every L_A is controlled by L_S; stage and guess counts each contribute at most one additional logarithmic factor.

assumptions: Fixed integer p>=2; public d>=1, L_p,D,mu,delta>0, w in X. G is C^(p-1) on an open neighborhood of X, Lip(D^(p-1)G)<=L_p on X, and mu-strongly monotone there. A continuous pth derivative and separate bounds on lower derivatives are not required.

An abstract residual interface A_{alpha,b} of Definition 5.1 is available: for every compatible monotone operator F and feasible x0 with some VI solution within a, it returns a verified (y,n,F(y)), y in X, n in N_X(y), ||F(y)+n||<=epsilon, including the already evaluated operator value, using at most C_p(1+Q_a^alpha)L_A(a,epsilon)^b queries.

Its implementation has a fixed public instance-independent leading constant and an interruptible prescribed cap. Even under a false distance promise, successful output must be verified and genuine. Every active ancestor cap is charged before each original-F query in all descendants; exhaustion immediately interrupts the capped call before an additional query, rather than checking after an uncontrolled subcall.

alpha>0 is fixed in the scope occurring in the paper; b is its fixed nonnegative logarithmic exponent. The conclusion is not a uniform assertion over arbitrary varying alpha or arbitrary unrelated residual procedures.

Use Algorithm 4 RestartTrial inside Algorithm 3 AdaptiveStrong. Each radius guess starts from original w. Normals belong to original N_X throughout; X is not replaced by an artificial ball. Exact feasible order-p jets and Section 3.2 internal operations define the resource model.
statement.conclusion: AdaptiveStrong(RestartTrial(A_{alpha,b}),G,w,mu,delta) returns (y,n,G(y)), y in X, n in N_X(y), saved evaluated G(y), and ||G(y)+n||<=delta, using at most C_p[1+(L_p r^(p-1)/mu)^alpha]L_S(mu,delta)^(b+2) original queries. This is equation (5.4) with gamma=alpha and logarithmic power b+2. At r=0 use its additive constant convention. The unknown-radius bound belongs to the complete composition, not one standalone RestartTrial.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Finite-dimensional Euclidean R^d; vector Euclidean and multilinear operator norms. Known nonempty compact convex X with diam(X)<=D, D>0. N_X(x)={n:<n,u-x><=0 for all u in X}. G has unique VI solution zstar. For 0<a<=D and epsilon>0, Q_a=L_p a^p/epsilon, L_A(a,epsilon)=1+log(2+D/a+Q_a). kappa_D=L_p D^(p-1)/mu; L_S(mu,delta)=1+log(2+kappa_D+L_p D^p/delta+mu D/delta). All log arguments are dimensionless. r=||w-zstar|| is analysis-only, never input.
statement.parameter_domains: p integer >=2; fixed alpha>0 as occurring in the paper, fixed b>=0; d>=1; L_p,D,mu,delta>0; w in X; 0<=r<=D. Fixed-exponent constants are known implementation constants independent of the instance.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every fixed admissible residual implementation and exponents in this scope, and every compatible strongly monotone G and public input, the stated composition supplies S_{alpha,b+2}. Its inherited guarantee is the certified interface guarantee, with no additional failure probability introduced by the wrappers. No random distance estimate or observed solution distance is used.

summary: An abstract capped residual interface yields a strong interface through RestartTrial composed with AdaptiveStrong, preserving the condition exponent and adding two logarithmic powers.
title: Lemma 5.3: capped residual restart yields a distance-adaptive strong solver
use_when: Convert an available residual solver into the next strong-solver interface without supplying its true initial distance.
